s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant patient with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
In eighth month of gestation
Palpitations lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure was 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate was 120 beats/min
Jugular venous pulsations revealed regular cannon waves
Auscultation was significant for a variable first heart sound
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG showed regular narrow QRS tachycardia at a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

raw.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant patient with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
In eighth month of gestation
Palpitations lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure was 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate was 120 beats/min
Jugular venous pulsations revealed regular cannon waves
Auscultation was significant for a variable first heart sound
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG showed regular narrow QRS tachycardia at a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

differentials: right atrial standstill with left atrial tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min and regular P waves marching onto QRS complexes, which is consistent with atrial tachycardia. The presence of regular cannon waves in the jugular venous pulsations and a variable first heart sound also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: arrhythmia
rejected.why: Too broad, as arrhythmia is a general term that encompasses many types of irregular heart rhythms, including atrial tachycardia

rejected.label: wolff parkinson white syndrome
rejected.why: Typically characterized by a delta wave on the ECG, which is not mentioned in the patient's ECG findings

rejected.label: ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: Characterized by a wide QRS complex, which is not present in the patient's ECG

rejected.label: atrioventricular dissociation
rejected.why: Typically characterized by a lack of association between P waves and QRS complexes, which is not present in the patient's ECG
